text.en: Prior to the introduction of Batchelor's romanization system, written Ainu in Japan was recorded, if at all, using the Japanese kana syllabary ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--kana-writing-prior-to-batchelor⟧.
text.ja: バチェラーのローマ字表記法の導入以前、日本国内においてアイヌ語は書かれるとしても日本語の仮名文字で表記されていた⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--kana-writing-prior-to-batchelor⟧。

text.en: In Batchelor's romanization system, Ainu *ci* [tʃi] is written as *chi*, and palatalized *s* is written as *sh* ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-batchelor-s-romanization-system-ainu-ci-t⟧. Batchelor, Kindaichi, and Chiri Yukie all made use of voiced stop letters *b*, *d*, and *g* in addition to voiceless *p*, *t*, and *k* in their romanized orthographies ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--batchelor-kindaichi-and-chiri-yukie-all-made-use⟧. In Chiri (1942), syllable-initial *h* and syllable-final *x* were analyzed as two distinct consonant phonemes within a twelve-consonant inventory ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-chiri-1942-syllable-initial-h-and-syllable⟧.
text.ja: バチェラーのローマ字表記法では、アイヌ語の*ci* [tʃi]を*chi*で表し、口蓋化した*s*を*sh*で表す⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-batchelor-s-romanization-system-ainu-ci-t⟧。バチェラー、金田一京助、知里幸恵の表記はいずれも、無声音*p*、*t*、*k*のほかに有声音*b*、*d*、*g*も用いている⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--batchelor-kindaichi-and-chiri-yukie-all-made-use⟧。知里（1942）では、*h*と*x*は12ある子音音素の中で互いに別の音素として位置づけられていた⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-chiri-1942-syllable-initial-h-and-syllable⟧。

text.en: Ainu phonemically has words without final vowels, including after *-r-*, although Batchelor often erroneously recorded final vowels on them ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--ainu-phonemically-has-words-without-final-vowels-including⟧. Whereas Chiri Yukie's orthography, established in Ainu Shin'yōshū (1923), distinguishes syllable-final *-r* from *r* followed by a vowel — a distinction Nakagawa (2024) identifies as the first clear such separation and as the basis of standard orthographic practice — Batchelor's orthography writes all instances as *r* followed by a vowel, for example *nukara* for *nukar* and *pirika* for *pirka* ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--yukie-chiri-1923-in-ainu-shin-y-sh⟧⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--whereas-chiri-yukie-s-orthography-distinguishes-syllable-final⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語は音素的には*-r-*の後を含め語末母音を持たない語があるが、バチェラーはそうした語にしばしば誤って語末母音を記録している⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--ainu-phonemically-has-words-without-final-vowels-including⟧。知里幸恵（1923）『アイヌ神謡集』において音節末の*-r*と*r*＋母音が初めて明確に区別され、これが標準の表記となったとされるが⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--yukie-chiri-1923-in-ainu-shin-y-sh⟧、バチェラーの表記ではそれらがすべて*r*＋母音で書かれており、たとえば*nukar*が*nukara*、*pirka*が*pirika*と記される⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--whereas-chiri-yukie-s-orthography-distinguishes-syllable-final⟧。

text.en: Forms in older records of the Tokachi dialect transcribed as *ruwe sitapan* are proposed by Nakagawa (2024) to be analyzed as *ru estap an* ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--forms-in-older-records-of-the-tokachi-dialect⟧.
text.ja: 十勝方言の過去の記録に*ruwe sitapan*とあるものは、中川（2024）によって*ru estap an*と分析すべきであると提案されている⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--forms-in-older-records-of-the-tokachi-dialect⟧。

text.en: Refsing (1986) asserts that Batchelor's dictionary and the grammar preceding it are extremely inaccurate and cannot be relied upon as primary sources for the study of Ainu, though they contain usable material when approached critically ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--batchelor-s-dictionary-and-the-grammar-preceding-it⟧. In a number of instances in Batchelor's dictionary, the English glosses are much closer to the actual meaning than the Japanese translations, which are totally misleading ⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-a-number-of-instances-in-batchelor-s⟧.
text.ja: レフシング（1986）は、バチェラーの辞書およびそれに先行する文法論は極めて不正確であり、アイヌ語研究の第一資料としては信頼できないが、批判的に扱えば有用な資料も含んでいると主張する⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--batchelor-s-dictionary-and-the-grammar-preceding-it⟧。また、バチェラーの辞書では日本語訳が完全に誤解を招くものである一方、英語訳のほうがはるかに実際の意味に近い例が散見される⟦claim:sources/historical-orthographies-and-the-batchelor-tradition--in-a-number-of-instances-in-batchelor-s⟧。
